 SCCH-23 3 MVC-3983/2020  JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 02.09.2020 at about 9.30 p.m, when the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EM-3426 which was ridden by his friend by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When they reached near KSRTC Quarters Guest House, 36th Cross, Jayanagar, 4th Block, Bengaluru City, at that time respondent No.3 being the driver of Karnataka State Government Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-GB-0066 drove the same in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent clinical examinations and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that, at the time of accident he was working in private company and also doing real estate business and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.

It is further urged that the MICO Layout Traffic police have registered a case in their Crime No.43/2020 against the petitioner's motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EM-3426, on the complaint given by the respondent No.3 and refused to receive complaint by the petitioner herein.
Hence the respondent No.1 to 5 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.5, the respondent No.5 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence she placed exparte.

sentences.text: After service of notice, respondent No.1 / KGID appeared through Special Government Counsel and filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
Further it is contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
It is admitted that the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-GB-0066 belonging to Secretary, Karnataka Mahiti Ayoga, Mahiti Soudha, Bengaluru and the insurance policy is valid as on the date of accident.
Further it is denied the negligence on the part of the driver of its vehicle.
Per contra it is contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of rider of motorcycle and the said rider drove the vehicle without possessing valid DL on the date of accident.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.

Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
5.
After service of notice, respondent No.2 /Secretary - RC owner of Innova car filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
Further it is contended that the petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties.

Further it is admitted the involvement of the vehicle in the accident and contended this respondent being the owner of the Toyota Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-GB-0066 and the said car is being used by this respondent for official purpose.

It is contended that on the date, time and place of accident the driver of Toyota Innova car was driving the same on the left side of the road in slowly by observing all the traffic rules at that time one Bhaskar was driving the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EM-3456 in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly applied the brakes and fell down.
On account of the fall, the bike skidded on the road road and dashed against the car, due to which the car suffered damages.
The jurisdictional police have registered a case in Crime No.43/2020 against the rider of the motorcycle / Bhaskar.
The driver of the Innova car is having valid Driving Licence and the insurance policy is valid on the date of accident.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. After service of notice, respondent No.3 /Driver of Innova car filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.

Further he admitted the involvement of the vehicle in the accident and contended that he was driving Toyota Innova car on the left side of the road in slowly by observing all the traffic rules at that time the rider of motorcycle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly applied the brakes, lost control and the motorcycle skidded, dragged some distance and dashed against the right side middle portion of the Innova car.
The jurisdictional police have registered a case in Crime No.43/2020 against the rider of the motorcycle / Bhaskar.
He admitted that he is having valid Driving Licence and same is valid on the date of accident.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. After service of notice, respondent No.4/United India Ins.Co.Ltd., filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EM-3426.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent denied the negligence on the part of the driver of Innova car and the petitioner is put to strict proof of the same.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES

1 ) Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a Road Traffic accident on 02.09.2020 at about 9.30 p.m, near KSRTC Quarters Guest House, 36th Cross, Jayanagar, 4th Block, Bengaluru City, and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Toyota Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-GB-0066 ?
2) Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation amount claimed ?

If so from whom and to what extent ?
3) What order or award ?
9. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 11 were marked on his behalf.
The respondents did not choose to lead any evidence on its behalf.
10. Heard counsel for the petitioner.
In spite of sufficient opportunity has been granted the advocate for petitioner, respondent No.1, 3 and 4 have not addressed their arguments.
On 27.06.2025 again and again called out, no representation.
Lastly called out at 4.45 p.m, and no representation.
Arguments of petitioner, respondent No.1, 3 and 4 is taken as nil.
Further they are liberty to file written arguments till before two days of pronouncement of judgment.
The counsel for respondent No.3 and 4 filed written arguments.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

11. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 12. ISSUE NO.1: The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation.

There is no dispute regarding the occurrence of the accident on the relevant date,
time and place.
The petitioner sustained injuries in the Road Traffic Accident is also not in conflict.
The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.

The question as to who was responsible for the accident has to be answered by looking into the evidence on record, perusal of which makes it evident that the rider of the motorcycle in which the petitioner proceeding as pillion rider.

The rider was proceeding on the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and they reached near KSRTC Quarters Guest House, 36th Cross,
Jayanagar, 4th Block, Bengaluru City,

at that time respondent No.3 being the driver of Karnataka State Government Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-GB-0066 drove the same in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused B.N. sentences.text: 13. The respondent No.1 to 3 denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the Innova car and further the respondent No.4 being the insurer of motorcycle also denied the negligence on the part of the Innova car.
Further it is contended that as per FIR it clearly discloses the jurisdictional police have registered a case in Crime No.43/2020 against the rider of the motorcycle / Bhaskar.

On careful perusal of these documents it appears that based on the information given by respondent No.3 / driver of Innova car the MICO Layout Traffic Police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 against the rider of motorcycle / respondent No.5.
This Court gave anxious consideration on astuteness to the contents of the above said document.
14. Further it is noteworthy to state that the petitioner has mainly relied on Ex.P.1 being the FIR and Ex.P.2 being the Complaint and they are police documents.
Except these two documents the petitioner has not produced spot mahazar, sketch, IMV Report, wound certificate and charge sheet before this Court.
During the course of cross examination by respondent No.3 counsel, the PW.1 stated that :

The counsel for respondent No.3 / driver of car filed written arguments stated that the MICO Layout Traffic Police registered the FIR against the rider of motorcycle in their crime No.43/2020 and after thorough investigation filed a charge sheet and it was registered in C.C.No.5830/2020 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC.

Further this Court on going through the Case Status :
Search by FIR Number, wherein Metropolitan Magistrate Traffic Court-IV, Bengaluru filed CC.5830/2020 against Bhashar and he pleaded guilty and paid fine before the Court.
As such this Court cannot found fault with the version of the petitioner herein.

Consequently this Tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused only due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-EM-3426 and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-GB-0066.
On assessing entire evidence the light of oral and documentary proof, the preponderance of probability tilts infavour of petitioner herein.

sentences.text:
: As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries :
X-ray shows right distal end radius fracture with right iliac wing fracture with right clavicle fracture.
Ex.P3 being the Out patient records and Ex.P.4 being the Discharge Summary of Sanjay Gandhi Hospital discloses that the petitioner was taken treatment from 03.09.2020 to 15.09.2020 for a period of (13 days).

During the course of treatment he underwent surgeries in the form of :
Conservative for Clavicle and Iliac wing CRIF with K-wire done on 08.09.2020 under BPB.

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
17. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :
The petitioner has deposed that he was working in private company and also doing real estate business and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
In order to prove the said fact she has produced Salary slips at Ex.P.10.
Except this the petitioner has not produced bank account statement or any other documents before this Court.
However he has neither proved his avocation nor his earning capacity.
However he has neither examined the doctor nor produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
During the course of his cross examination he categorically admitted as he had sustained injuries in the accident and he left the job.
Further he has not produced any letter regarding to submit his resignation and in turn his office had issued termination letter.
Further he admitted that he can produce the Bank statement but he has not done so.
The PW.1 admitted that now he was working in Soch Apparels in Tumkur.
In view of the decision reported in ILR 2010 KAR 2439, 'If the claimant has continued in service, then the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.'
The elicitations brought during the course of cross-examination of PW.1 also make it clear that he has not suffered any financial loss during his treatment period.

Therefore no compensation can be awarded to the petitioner under the heads 'loss of future income' & 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
18.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 13 days is proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take his care by leaving their duties.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,000/- per day and a sum of Rs.13,000/- (1,000 X 13) is awarded under this head.
19. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
20. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the bills marked at Ex.P6, he has spent Rs.250/-, as per Ex.P.9 he has spent Rs.450/-, and as per Ex.P.11 he has spent Rs.20,592/- towards medical expenses.

sentences.text: he spent Rs.21,292/-.
During the course of his cross examination she categorically admitted that he was covered under ESI and PF.
He denied the suggestion that he had got reimbursed the medical bills by the ESI.
All these bills have been examined with care and are found to be correct.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.21,292/- which is rounded off to Rs.21,300/- towards medical expenses.
21. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
22. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

23. The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Loss of future income due to : - Nil - disability 2 Loss of income during laid-up : - Nil - period 3 Attendant charges, extra nutritious : 13,000-00 food & conveyance charges 4 Pain & sufferings : 50,000-00 5 Medical expenses : 21,300-00 6 Loss of future amenities & : 40,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : - Nil - Total 1,24,300-00 24.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
25. In view of the discussion made in issue No.1 it is amply clear that the accident in question occurred due to the sole negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-EM-3426.

Hence the petition deserves to be dismissed against respondents No.1 to 3 i.e., insurer,
owner and driver of Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-GB-0066.
26.
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, the order sheet discloses that petitioner has taken ample opportunities to lead his evidence.
Hence for this idle period, no interest should accrue to the claimant.
To put it differently he should not be permitted to derive benefit from his own wrong.

Allowing interest even for the periods covered by the adjournment granted at the instance of the claimant, virtually amounts to unjust enrichment of the claimant at the cost of other stake holders, namely owners of B.N. 7 the offending vehicle or the Insurance companies.
27.

sentences.text: In this view of the matter, relying upon the ratio laid down by our Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.4427/2010 (DD on 12/07/2018), the Insurance Company cannot be saddled with payment of interest for the period for which there was delay on the part of the petitioner in proceeding with the petition.
Hence it is ordered that Insurance Company cannot be saddled with payment of interest for the period for which there is delay on the part of the petitioner in proceeding with the petition.
Thereby the interest for the period from the date of evidence of petitioner and till completion of evidence of petitioner is waived off.

Therefore, the respondent No.4 & 5 being the insurer and owner of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EM-3426 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondent No.4 being the insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EM- 3426 is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
28.
ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,24,300/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (interest is waived off from the stage of evidence of petitioner and till completion of evidence of petitioner).
Further he is entitled interest from the date of filing of petition till the date of evidence of petitioner and after the completion of evidence of petitioner till the realization.
The respondent No.4 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest of the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
The petition is dismissed against  respondent 1 to 3.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

However the respondent No.4 being the insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EM- 3426 is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Thereby the interest for the period from the date of evidence of petitioner and till completion of evidence of petitioner is waived off.
Therefore, the respondent No.4 & 5 being the insurer and owner of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-EM-3426 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
28.
ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,24,300/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (interest is waived off from the stage of evidence of petitioner and till completion of evidence of petitioner).
Further he is entitled interest from the date of filing of petition till the date of evidence of petitioner and after the completion of evidence of petitioner till the realization.
The respondent No.4 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest of the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
The petition is dismissed against  respondent 1 to 3.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
